set.body:
Current user direction

User correction 2026-09-12 supersedes earlier ownership framing: Eidolon is an early-stage idea and is not a current focus. This P3 proposal imposes no architecture, module retirement, migration or dependency requirement on ScalaFIM. Keep it dormant unless concrete native correctness/performance/API needs or an explicitly adopted consumer justify reopening implementation. Core ScalaFIM work and PHRF proceed independently. Historical ADR/RFE text is retained as proposal history, not binding authority. Sequential source assessment: WorkflowTypes still contains ArtifactLocation/WorkflowArtifactRef, but existing archive/estimates already provide reusable resource and pinned-identity boundaries. Any future consolidation should compare those native APIs and actual consumers before adding another descriptor family or removing live types. No foreign-adapter conformance is required for current native work.

Historical proposal

Context: WorkflowTypes.scala defines ArtifactLocation and WorkflowArtifactRef[A] inside scalafim.fmri.workflow. They mix reusable scientific resource identity with workflow branding and currently feed study catalogs, masks, BIDS compilation, result bundles, and JVM file resolution. Eidolon needs to resolve these through explicit adapters without importing a second workflow model.

Scope:
- Introduce transport-neutral typed resource descriptors in the lowest appropriate reusable module, separating logical scientific identity from physical URI/location and access capability.
- Cover BIDS projects, BOLD images, events/confounds tables, masks, and result manifests without embedding scheduler, cache, publication, or run state.
- Keep file/URI/object-store resolution in JVM adapter capabilities; shared descriptors remain serializable on JVM and Scala.js.
- Migrate WorkflowArtifactRef and ArtifactLocation consumers, then remove the workflow-branded types.
- Define the adapter contract by which eidolon artifact references resolve to scalafim resource descriptors and returned scientific outputs are published by eidolon.

Acceptance:
- Descriptor equality and canonical encoding are deterministic.
- Shared round-trip tests pass on JVM and Scala.js.
- No shared descriptor captures an open reader, filesystem Path, closure, credentials, or application lifecycle state.
- A conformance test proves eidolon-to-scalafim input resolution and output handoff without a reverse build dependency.

Downstream consumer: eidolon artifact/module adapters; tracking issue bd-01KXYH4NRMFGV41W48AD6N5Y0P.
set.title: [DORMANT PROPOSAL] Consolidate resource descriptors if native reuse warrants it
